name: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
note: Unit and topic structure (units 8-13, 31 topics, and their numbering) follows the College Board AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2024; the copy on AP Central carries minor clarifications for 2026-27), retrieved 2026-11-21 from https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-physics-c-electricity-and-magnetism-course-and-exam-description.pdf and https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-physics-c-electricity-and-magnetism-course-at-a-glance.pdf (unit list also on https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/courses/ap-physics-c-electricity-and-magnetism). Titles and descriptions are written in Scorpio's own words; they are not College Board text.

units.title: Electric charges, fields and Gauss's law
units.summary: Charge, Coulomb's law, fields of point charges and continuous distributions, electric flux and Gauss's law.

topics.title: Electric charge and electric force
topics.summary: Two kinds of charge, the inverse-square force between point charges, vector sums of forces and the permittivity of a medium.

topics.title: Conservation of electric charge and charging
topics.summary: Charge is neither made nor lost: charging by friction, contact and induction, and grounding.

topics.title: Electric fields
topics.summary: Field as force per unit charge: field vectors, field lines and superposition for point charges.

topics.title: Electric fields of charge distributions
topics.summary: Integrating over lines, rings, arcs and other continuous charge, using symmetry to drop components.

topics.title: Electric flux
topics.summary: How much field passes through a surface: the area vector, orientation and the surface integral.

topics.title: Gauss's law
topics.summary: Net flux through a closed surface and the charge inside it; fields of spheres, cylinders and planes of charge.

units.title: Electric potential
units.summary: Potential energy of charge systems, potential as an integral of the field, and energy conservation.

topics.title: Electric potential energy
topics.summary: Energy stored in a system of charges and the work needed to assemble or rearrange it.

topics.title: Electric potential
topics.summary: Potential energy per unit charge for point charges and distributions, equipotentials, and the field as the negative slope of potential.

topics.title: Conservation of electric energy
topics.summary: Speed and energy changes of charges that move through a potential difference.

units.title: Conductors and capacitors
units.summary: Charge and field on conductors in equilibrium, sharing charge between conductors, capacitance and dielectrics.

topics.title: Electrostatics with conductors
topics.summary: Zero field inside, excess charge on the surface, constant potential throughout, and shielding.

topics.title: Redistribution of charge between conductors
topics.summary: Charge moves between connected conductors until they share one potential; induced charge and grounding.

topics.title: Capacitors
topics.summary: Capacitance from geometry, the field between plates and the energy a charged capacitor stores.

topics.title: Dielectrics
topics.summary: How an insulator between the plates changes capacitance, field, potential difference and stored energy.

units.title: Electric circuits
units.summary: Current, resistance, power, series and parallel circuits, Kirchhoff's rules and RC circuits with calculus.

topics.title: Electric current
topics.summary: Current as the rate of charge flow, current density, drift speed and conventional direction.

topics.title: Simple circuits
topics.summary: Closed loops, circuit diagrams and the roles of batteries, wires, switches and loads.

topics.title: Resistance, resistivity and Ohm's law
topics.summary: What sets an object's resistance, and the current through ohmic and non-ohmic elements.

topics.title: Electric power
topics.summary: The rate at which circuit elements transfer or dissipate energy.

topics.title: Compound direct current circuits
topics.summary: Equivalent resistance for series and parallel combinations, meters and internal resistance.

topics.title: Kirchhoff's loop rule
topics.summary: Energy conservation around any closed loop of a circuit.

topics.title: Kirchhoff's junction rule
topics.summary: Charge conservation where branches of a circuit meet.

topics.title: Resistor-capacitor (RC) circuits
topics.summary: Equivalent capacitance, and charging and discharging through a resistor: the differential equation, exponential solutions and the time constant.

units.title: Magnetic fields and electromagnetism
units.summary: Magnetic fields, forces on moving charges and currents, the Biot-Savart law and Ampère's law.

topics.title: Magnetic fields
topics.summary: Properties of magnetic fields, dipoles, field lines that close on themselves and how materials respond to a field.

topics.title: Magnetism and moving charges
topics.summary: The cross-product force on a charge moving through a field, circular paths, the Hall effect and the field a moving charge makes.

topics.title: Magnetic fields of current-carrying wires and the Biot-Savart law
topics.summary: Integrating current elements for the field of wires and loops; forces on and between wires.

topics.title: Ampère's law
topics.summary: The field around a closed path and the current through it; long wires, solenoids and other symmetric currents.

units.title: Electromagnetic induction
units.summary: Magnetic flux, Faraday's and Lenz's laws, forces on induced currents, inductance, and LR and LC circuits.

topics.title: Magnetic flux
topics.summary: How much magnetic field passes through an area, including fields that vary across it.

topics.title: Electromagnetic induction
topics.summary: Faraday's law: emf from the rate of change of flux, with Lenz's law for its direction.

topics.title: Induced currents and magnetic forces
topics.summary: Forces on conductors that carry induced current: rods and loops moving through a field.

topics.title: Inductance
topics.summary: An inductor opposes changes in its current; inductance of a solenoid and energy stored in its field.

topics.title: Circuits with resistors and inductors (LR circuits)
topics.summary: Current that grows or decays exponentially: initial and long-time behaviour and the time constant.

topics.title: Circuits with capacitors and inductors (LC circuits)
topics.summary: Charge and current that oscillate as energy passes between capacitor and inductor.
